title: Articles, nouns and quantifiers
subtitle: a/an, the, zero article, countable and uncountable nouns, many/much/few/little

blocks.text: There are two indefinite articles in English: **a** and **an**. **An** is used before vowel sounds.

rows.use: Singular countable nouns (when we are not being specific or when we mention something for the first time)
rows.example: There's **a** good film on TV tonight.

blocks.text: Whether we use **an** or **a** depends on the **sound**, not the spelling.
blocks.note: The news is on TV in **an** hour. · Being in a film was **a unique** experience for me.

blocks.text: There is one definite article in English: **the**.

rows.use: Singular countable nouns (when we are being specific)
rows.example: Where's **the** DVD you were talking about?

rows.use: Singular countable nouns (when we are talking generally)
rows.example: **The** radio seemed amazing to people at first.

rows.use: Plural countable nouns (when we are being specific)
rows.example: I didn't believe **the** rumours about the prime minister.

rows.use: Uncountable nouns (when we are being specific)
rows.example: I followed **the** advice my lawyer gave me.

blocks.text: The way we say **the** changes depending on the sound at the start of the next word. Before a consonant sound (**the media, the USA, the programme**), we pronounce it /ðə/. Before a vowel sound (**the announcer, the actor, the editor**), we pronounce it /ði/.
We often use **the** when something is unique or there is only one of it.
blocks.note: **the** sky, **the** sun, **the** moon, **the** Prince of Wales, **the** North Pole, **the** World Cup

blocks.text: We often don't use an article at all. This is sometimes called the **zero article**.

rows.use: Plural countable nouns (when we are talking generally)
rows.example: Journalists often face dangerous situations.

rows.use: Uncountable nouns (when we are talking generally)
rows.example: News travels fast these days.
definite: **in the 1990s, in (the) summer, in the morning** · zero: **in 2008, in June, on Friday, at night**
indefinite: **have a job, work as a …** · definite: **the queen, the principal, the president, the French** · zero: **become president, go to work, be at work, have work to do, be French**

definite: **the Alps, the Atlantic Ocean, the River Thames, the Earth, the Arctic, the USA, the UK, the Cyclades** · zero: **Mount Everest, Paris, America, Mars/Venus/Jupiter etc., Oxford Street, Lake Superior, Crete**
definite: **the media, on the radio, play the guitar, go to the cinema, watch (the) TV** · zero: **listen to music, on television, play tennis/football etc.**
definite: **the army, the police, the fire brigade**
definite: **go to the school** (as a visitor), **be in the first year** · zero: **go to school** (as a student), **be in Class 3B, maths**
indefinite: **take a taxi, catch a/the bus** · definite: **on the bus** · zero: **on foot, go home, go by bus**
indefinite: **have a cold/headache/cough** · definite: **have (the) flu/measles** · zero: **have toothache**
definite: **the bank, the tax office, go to the hospital/prison** (as a visitor) · zero: **go to hospital/prison/church** (as a patient/prisoner/worshipper)

items: Speakers of American English do not usually use **hospital** without an article: US *The ambulance took Simon to the hospital.* · UK *The ambulance took Simon to hospital.*

rows.use: Countable nouns · a/the, some, many · singular or plural verb
rows.example: I want to be **a journalist**. · Where is **the newspaper**? · There are **some good articles** in the paper. · How **many channels** do you get?

rows.use: Uncountable nouns · the, some, much · singular verb
rows.example: Did you hear **the news**? · **Some important news** has just come in. · How **much information** do we have about it? · Your **advice was** very useful.

blocks.text: Most uncountable nouns are singular, but a few are plural. These include **clothes, scissors, jeans, spectacles, trousers, groceries**, etc. With these words, we use a plural verb.
blocks.note: Oh, no! My new **clothes are** dirty!

blocks.text: Some nouns are countable with one meaning and uncountable with another.
blocks.note: Do you think you could bring me **a clean glass**? (countable) · We should make computer monitors out of recycled **glass**. (uncountable)

rows.use: many · countable nouns, usually in negative statements and questions
rows.example: There aren't **many** programmes on TV that I find interesting.

rows.use: much · uncountable nouns, usually in negative statements and questions
rows.example: My dad never shows **much** interest in the news.

rows.use: a lot of / lots of · countable and uncountable nouns in positive statements
rows.example: That film has won **a lot of / lots of** awards. · What **a lot of** luggage you've got!
There have been **a few** scandals in the papers recently.
They say that **a little** knowledge is a dangerous thing.
Richard has **few** interests outside work.
The police have **little** information about the robbery.

blocks.text: The phrase **only a few** means 'not many'. The phrase **only a little** means 'not much'.
blocks.note: There are **only a few** programmes on TV that I like watching. · There's **only a little** sugar left, so get some when you go out.

exercises.title: E · Newsflash!
exercises.instruction: Tap the word that is wrong, then write the correction.
exercises.paragraph: We interrupt your usual schedule to bring you an {click:important news}. We are receiving {click:informations} about a spaceship that has landed outside the White House. The large ship seems to be made of {click:glasses}. Reports say that a short time ago aliens came out of the craft. Eye-witnesses described them as short and said their clothes {click:was} made of metal and their {click:hairs} was bright green. Strangely, one of them appeared to be wearing {click:a jean}. {click:Much people} said that they seemed to be friendly. The President of the United States is currently holding a meeting with the visitors in the hope that we can exchange {click:knowledges}. Police {click:advices} are to stay indoors and under no circumstances approach the spaceship. We will be back with {click:another news} as soon as we can. And now back to your usual programme, Gardening for Beginners.
